description.p: Kaller turns a paired Bluetooth phone into a phone you can answer from your desktop. Calls stay on the phone and on the mobile network. Kaller sends the commands and carries the audio, so you can keep the phone in your pocket.

ul.li: Dial a number, answer a call, and end a call.
Search your contacts by name or by number, including keypad search.
Read the contacts and the call history from the phone.
Hold one call and answer another, swap between two calls, and join them.
Mute the microphone, set the speaker level, and send keypad tones.
Open a telephone link from any other application.

description.p: Kaller needs PipeWire with telephony support, BlueZ, and a phone that is paired and connected over the hands-free profile.
Foner is now Kaller. Settings and contacts move over on the first start.

The selected phone no longer changes when another phone leaves. Mute shows the phone's answer. Clearing contacts also clears the dialled numbers. The call history imports once per phone. Contacts can come from KDE Connect.
